A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. Their text, equations, four figures, and appendices A–H are readable and matchable despite the conference reformatting.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix H report original transformer training and evaluation results on synthetic Gaussian-mixture classification tasks.

after.justification: Section 5 and Appendix H retain original transformer experiments and report an additional LDA comparison.

M1.justification: The transformer architecture, sparse parameterization, sigmoid/softmax outputs, losses, and training and inference procedures remain unchanged. LDA is introduced as a comparator and interpretation of the existing model.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic Gaussian-mixture classification tasks, including the unequal-norm and varying-covariance scenarios. The LDA comparison uses the existing three-class task.

E2.justification: Figure 3 substantially replaces the classical comparator set: linear-kernel SVM, Gaussian-kernel SVM, 1-NN, and 3-NN are removed, and LDA is added. Softmax regression and the three transformer variants remain.

E3.justification: Appendix H.2 retains the data generation, training budgets, model configurations, optimizers, prompt-length settings, and evaluation over 20 queries with 100 prompts each. No protocol revision is documented for the changed Figure 2(a) results.

E4.justification: Figure 2(a) revises the single-layer transformer's unequal-norm robustness curve and shaded band. The tested question and conclusion that three-layer transformers tolerate this shift better remain unchanged; the other sensitivity studies are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report three repetitions with different seeds for Figures 1–3 and ten for Figure 4, and both display shaded bands. No new uncertainty definitions, significance tests, or statistical procedures are reported.

E6.justification: Under unchanged documented settings, Figure 2(a)'s single-layer unequal-norm error changes from approximately 0.26 to 0.21 at M=20 and 0.21 to 0.16 at M=100. Figure 3 removes four baseline curves and adds LDA, whose error approaches the transformer curves as context grows. The main empirical trends persist, and Figures 1 and 4 are identical.

T1.justification: The principal bounds and appendix proofs remain unchanged. Theorems 3.3 and 4.3 make positive curvature and finite smoothness explicit. The relocated Remark E.1, now Remark 3.7, reverses the quadratic mean-offset sign in its posterior formula, although the following z definition retains the old sign.

C1.justification: The introduction withdraws the claim of being first to study transformer training dynamics for Gaussian-mixture classification, retains the multiclass convergence novelty claim, and adds approximate implementation of LDA as a contribution. The headline convergence and inference-error claims remain.

C2.justification: New Remark 3.8 explains the covariance and equal-norm assumptions through LDA and attributes the short-context advantage to covariance information learned during pretraining. It also explains LDA's narrowing performance gap at longer contexts. The existing failure-condition discussion is largely relocated from Remark E.1 to Remark 3.7.

D1.justification: Appendix H.2 preserves the implementation library, architecture details, hyperparameters, data construction, and evaluation instructions. No LDA-specific implementation settings or new code/data access information are supplied.

R1.justification: The introduction and Appendix A add Frei and Vardi (2024), distinguishing its stated signal-to-noise assumptions and binary setting. Appendix A also adds five works on transformer convergence, vision transformers, and sparse selection, while retaining the existing literature.

P1.justification: There are targeted abstract and introduction edits, an added LDA explanation, expanded related work, relocation of Remark E.1, and new acknowledgements and an impact statement. Most prose and the overall section and proof organization remain intact.

P2.justification: The main text changes from a single-column draft to an ICML two-column layout, extensively reflowing equations and figures. Figures 2–3 have revised axis ranges, typography, and legends, and Figure 4 moves to a separate appendix page.

improvement.justification: v3 improves research positioning by acknowledging directly related Gaussian-mixture work and narrowing its novelty claim. The relevant LDA baseline and explanation also clarify what pretraining contributes. These are limited gains: four earlier baselines disappear, reproducibility information is unchanged, and the new LDA remark contains a factor-of-two error in its empirical mean-difference expression. The main theoretical results remain intact.
